program.name: ANEVUM Mathematics & Theory
program.purpose: Develop mathematically explicit, falsifiable models of adaptive decision-making and convert useful results into bounded RHEN research without granting theory any production authority.

standards.name: PROVENANCE
standards.rule: Every mathematical claim is labeled as known mathematics, an ANEVUM application, an extension candidate, a conjecture, or an independently verified original result.

standards.name: FALSIFIABILITY
standards.rule: Applied conjectures must state assumptions, measurable consequences, and a failure condition before experiment execution.

standards.name: SEPARATION
standards.rule: Theory may propose models and experiments but cannot mutate live strategy, risk, sizing, execution, broker state, validation gates, holdout access, or promotion state.

standards.name: REPRODUCIBILITY
standards.rule: Derivations, simulations, experiment links, source commits, and evidence references must be durable and reconstructable.

standards.name: NEGATIVE_RESULTS
standards.rule: Disproofs, failed derivations, null results, and rejected hypotheses remain part of the permanent research record.

tracks.name: Adaptive Systems Mathematics
tracks.scope: Stochastic processes, sequential inference, online learning, control, optimization, information theory, and market microstructure with RHEN as the first applied laboratory.

tracks.name: Pure & Foundational Mathematics
tracks.scope: Independent study and original problem work in areas such as number theory, combinatorics, geometry, topology, logic, and related foundations, without requiring an immediate trading application.

tracks.name: Computational Mathematics & Verification
tracks.scope: Symbolic and numerical experimentation, proof assistance, counterexample search, reproducible simulation, and machine-verifiable checks where appropriate.

problems.title: Adaptive Inference Under Nonstationarity
problems.question: Given a partially observed, nonstationary stochastic environment with switching costs, transaction costs, delay, noise, and finite capital, how should an adaptive system decide when apparent change is real enough to justify changing its decision policy?

formalization.target_bound: Derive non-vacuous performance or regret bounds whose dependence on environmental variation, observation noise, switching cost, and market frictions is explicit.

assumptions: No universal market predictor is assumed to exist.
The latent state is only partially observed through noisy, delayed measurements.
The environment may change and the rate of change is not known in advance.
Changing policy has an explicit cost, including false regime changes.
Any trading application must include observable transaction costs, slippage assumptions, liquidity constraints, and finite-capital limits.
non_claims: ATP-001 does not claim that markets are predictable in general.
ATP-001 does not claim that a mathematical proof implies profitability.
ATP-001 cannot authorize a live strategy change or bypass RHEN development, validation, holdout, shadow, or promotion gates.

workstreams.title: Latent-state representation
workstreams.objective: Define state variables that capture exploitable structure without encoding future information or unstable retrospective labels.

workstreams.title: Sequential change evidence
workstreams.objective: Measure evidence for persistent structural change while controlling false alarms under dependent, heteroskedastic observations.

workstreams.title: Switching-cost control
workstreams.objective: Derive when the expected value of adapting exceeds transaction, model, operational, and false-switch costs.

workstreams.title: Dynamic regret
workstreams.objective: Study regret relative to a changing comparator under unknown variation budgets and realistic feedback delays.

workstreams.title: Information value
workstreams.objective: Quantify whether new observations materially reduce decision uncertainty before additional complexity is admitted.

workstreams.title: Market frictions
workstreams.objective: Translate theoretical guarantees into bounds that explicitly degrade with spreads, slippage, liquidity, latency, and capital constraints.

conjectures.title: Evidence-adjusted switching threshold
conjectures.statement: For a bounded family of nonstationary latent-state models with positive switching cost, an optimal or near-optimal adaptation rule can be expressed as an evidence threshold that increases with switching cost and false-alarm loss and decreases with the expected persistence and value of the new regime.
conjectures.falsification: Disprove the threshold form in an admissible model class, or show that no threshold rule can match the best admissible non-threshold policy within a useful bound.

conjectures.title: Persistence-adjusted regime evidence
conjectures.statement: When change-point evidence is discounted by estimated regime persistence, adaptation can reduce false switches relative to evidence-only detection without materially increasing delay across a defined nonstationary model class.
conjectures.falsification: Show that persistence adjustment cannot improve the false-switch versus detection-delay frontier under the frozen model class and loss function.

conjectures.title: Value-of-information gate
conjectures.statement: A research or strategy-complexity increase should be admitted only when the expected decision value of the additional information exceeds its estimation, execution, and model-selection costs.
conjectures.falsification: Construct a valid setting in which the gate systematically rejects information that improves expected utility after all stated costs, or accepts information that cannot improve expected utility.

success_criteria: A precise model class with explicit assumptions and observability boundaries.
At least one theorem, impossibility result, or quantitatively useful bound that survives independent checking.
A simulation implementation that reproduces the theoretical result under controlled conditions.
A frozen RHEN experiment manifest linking any applied conjecture to canonical data without changing production behavior.
A permanent record of rejected conjectures and negative results.

results.title: Exact myopic switching thresholds in the symmetric two-state model
results.statement: In the one-period symmetric two-state decision model, positive switching cost creates exact upper and lower belief thresholds and a hysteresis interval of width kappa divided by the correct-versus-wrong reward spread.
results.scope: Restricted to the one-period symmetric binary-state, binary-action model. It does not prove ATP-001-C1 for general nonstationary partially observed environments.

problems.title: Discovery Reliability
problems.question: How much evidence must RHEN observe before it is justified in believing that an edge exists when hypotheses are searched adaptively, evidence is inspected repeatedly, observations are dependent, and market structure may change?

formalization.latent_state: candidate edge expectancy and research-search state
formalization.observation: normalized net candidate outcome Y_{h,i} in [-1,1]
formalization.action: continue observing, reject, confirm, replicate, or archive within protected research gates
formalization.target_bound: Construct a search-aware, anytime-valid evidence policy with explicit false-discovery control, effect-size evidence, temporal replication, and quantified decision delay.

assumptions: Candidate outcomes used by the v1 e-process are frozen before confirmation and normalized to the closed interval [-1,1].
The confirmatory null is conditional: E[Y_{h,i} | F_{i-1}] <= 0 for every eligible observation.
Betting fractions and mixture weights are predictable and cannot be selected after observing the outcome they score.
Every confirmatory experiment has a defined global information filtration and immutable methodology identity.
Development data may generate hypotheses but cannot also serve as untouched confirmatory evidence for those hypotheses.
Economic actionability is distinct from statistical detectability and requires a separate positive effect-size threshold.
non_claims: MATH-001 does not claim that any current RHEN strategy has a real edge.
MATH-001 does not set the final RHEN alpha, FDR target, effect-size threshold, betting mixture, or promotion policy.
MATH-001 does not authorize DEVELOPMENT, VALIDATION, HOLDOUT, quarantine access, or production changes.
The implemented B1 confidence sequence is intentionally conservative and is not claimed to be optimal.
No mathematical novelty is claimed for the fixed-lambda e-process, convex-mixture validity, or Ville/Hoeffding constructions.

The MATH-001 search ledger does not itself convert cumulative search exposure into a p-value, e-value penalty, FDR threshold, or production decision; that calibration belongs to later multiplicity work.

MATH-001-C does not freeze an organization-wide multiplicity policy, alpha level, or FDR target; implemented procedures remain study candidates until the reliability-policy workstream selects among them.
Unconditional zero mean is not sufficient for B1 validity; MATH-001-D requires the stated conditional-mean null relative to the global information filtration.
MATH-001-D dependence diagnostics do not by themselves certify the conditional null, independence, stationarity, or economic actionability.

workstreams.title: Search accounting
workstreams.objective: Define immutable hypothesis identity, family identity, search generation, and cumulative search exposure.

workstreams.title: Sequential evidence
workstreams.objective: Develop and verify anytime-valid e-processes and confidence sequences for candidate-edge evidence.

workstreams.title: Multiplicity
workstreams.objective: Compare familywise controls, e-BH, e-LOND, and conventional multiple-testing procedures under RHEN-style search.

workstreams.title: Dependence
workstreams.objective: Stress-test temporal dependence, cross-candidate dependence, heavy tails, and volatility clustering.

workstreams.title: Selection bias
workstreams.objective: Quantify development search and candidate-optimization bias.

workstreams.title: Nonstationarity
workstreams.objective: Measure regime concentration, temporal instability, decay, and replication failure.

workstreams.title: Simulation laboratory
workstreams.objective: Evaluate policies in known-truth worlds and quantify false discoveries, power, coverage, and decision delay.

workstreams.title: Reliability policy
workstreams.objective: Select the eventual RHEN evidence gate subject to frozen reliability constraints.

workstreams.title: Integration specification
workstreams.objective: Map proven research outputs into bounded Research Agent telemetry without production authority.

workstreams.title: Research Note 001
workstreams.objective: Maintain the complete derivation, empirical results, provenance, limitations, and rejected approaches.

conjectures.title: Reliability-constrained decision-delay improvement
conjectures.statement: There exists a reliability policy combining anytime-valid sequential evidence, explicit search exposure, multiple-testing control, and temporal replication that reduces expected decision delay relative to conservative fixed-sample baselines while satisfying the same frozen empirical false-discovery constraints across the MATH-001 simulation family.
conjectures.falsification: Under the frozen simulation family and loss function, fail to find any admissible policy with lower expected decision delay than the comparator set at matched reliability, or construct a valid counterexample showing the proposed architecture cannot satisfy its stated error constraints.

success_criteria: The statistical object called an edge has a precise conditional null and effect-size definition.
Search history and hypothesis-family identity are durably represented.
At least one anytime-valid evidence primitive is implemented and checked against its written assumptions.
Multiple-testing and global-filtration requirements are explicit.
Known-null calibration, power, coverage, and decision delay are measured in reproducible simulations.
Dependence, heavy tails, selection, and nonstationarity receive dedicated adversarial tests.
The final evidence policy is frozen only after comparator evaluation and retains zero production authority.

results.title: Fixed-lambda edge evidence process
results.statement: For normalized outcomes Y_i in [-1,1], predictable lambda in [0,1), and the conditional null E[Y_i | F_{i-1}] <= 0, E_n=product_i(1+lambda Y_i) is a nonnegative supermartingale and therefore an anytime-valid e-process.
results.scope: Known sequential-inference mathematics instantiated for the MATH-001 candidate-edge null. It does not establish that any RHEN candidate has positive expectancy.

results.title: Frozen convex-mixture edge evidence process
results.statement: A predeclared convex mixture of valid fixed-lambda e-processes remains a valid e-process, allowing one frozen evidence process to cover a range of effect scales without post-hoc lambda selection.
results.scope: Known closure property applied to the MATH-001 evidence construction. The currently implemented lambda grid is a study configuration, not a final RHEN policy.

results.title: Discovery-reliability evidence primitive
results.statement: MATH-001 now has an executable study-only evidence primitive combining a frozen mixture e-process, an anytime p-value summary, and a conservative simultaneous lower bound for running average conditional expectancy, plus a reproducible pure-null repeated-search simulation.
results.scope: Research-only implementation. It cannot confirm an edge, open protected research stages, or change RHEN production behavior.

results.title: Immutable hypothesis and search-exposure ledger
results.statement: RHEN research now assigns deterministic family and hypothesis identities, records every proposed scientific hypothesis and candidate configuration as append-only search exposure, preserves data-access and terminal events, and backfills prior rejected or terminal research so future multiplicity work does not begin from an artificial zero-search baseline.
results.scope: Research-accounting infrastructure only. The ledger does not itself impose a numerical multiple-testing penalty, confirm an edge, open a protected stage, access quarantine, or authorize production changes.

results.title: Multiplicity-control study engine
results.statement: RHEN research now has deterministic implementations of Bonferroni, Holm, BH, BY, base e-BH, e-LOND, and asynchronous e-LOND, with proposal-bound freeze-time multiplicity plans and a known-truth simulation benchmark.
results.scope: Research-only multiplicity infrastructure. Fixed-family and online procedures retain their stated dependence assumptions; the organization-wide alpha/FDR target and final reliability policy remain unfrozen.

results.title: Conditional-dependence validity framework
results.statement: RHEN research now distinguishes dependent processes that preserve the B1 conditional-mean null from unconditional-zero processes that violate it, freezes dependence stress requirements before methodology eligibility, records deterministic dependence plans, and provides known-truth temporal and cross-candidate dependence benchmarks.
results.scope: Research-only dependence infrastructure. Diagnostics do not prove martingale validity; raw unbounded outcomes remain outside the current B1 evidence contract; no final reliability policy is frozen.
